title: Canonical field-coefficient Weil compact support and shift data
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Use the rational and common-stage constructible categories and their geometric-Frobenius fixed pairs [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. For each scheme morphism with $\ell$ invertible, give the integral pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] its unique shift structure whose chain comparison is signed Roos reindexing $(x,y)\mapsto(x,(-1)^r y)$ and whose derived comparison descends through the retained good-resolution comparison of [lem-a1-integral-pullback-completed-comparison]. Restrict it to integral constructible objects. Give rational pullback the unique shift whose component at $1$ is the localization of this integral component; give common-stage pullback the unique shift whose component at $1$ on each pair is represented by that rational component. All integer components obey the usual zero and addition coherences.

For finite-type $k_0$-schemes $X_0,Y_0$ and $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$, let $P_f$ be rational pullback along the geometric-fibre morphism. Localize the integral composition comparisons of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition], and use geometric-Frobenius naturality of [def-zl-weil-ind-sheaf-category] to define $P_fF_X\simeq F_YP_f$. For a proper $p_0$, choose the right adjoint $R_p$ with its adjunction to $P_p$; for an open immersion $j_0$, choose the left adjoint $J_j$ with its adjunction to $P_j$. These adjoints exist on the rational constructible categories. The proper Frobenius exchange is the right mate of the inverse pullback square, and the inverse open exchange is the left mate of the pullback square. Both maps are invertible, as witnessed by inverse automorphism squares. Give $R_p$ and $J_j$ the shifts uniquely compatible with their adjunctions to the normalized pullback shifts.

For a compactification $c=(j_0,p_0)$ use the middle scheme and arrows of [def-zl-weil-compact-support-cohomology] and set $H_{f,c}=J_jR_p$ in diagrammatic order. Its Frobenius exchange is the composite of the proper and open exchanges with the ordinary associators, and its shift is the composite of their adjunction shifts. For separated finite-type $f_0$, this functor is naturally isomorphic on every object and morphism to the normalized rational compact-support functor [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] for every geometric compactification. At $\Omega$ reuse exactly the proper/open functors and exchange of [def-zl-common-stage-weil-shriek], giving them the same adjunction-mate shifts from normalized common-stage pullback. These are presentations of the exact compact-support operation of [lem-zl-field-shriek-lower-bound]. No separatedness of the structure morphisms is assumed; scheme and algebraic-closure universes are independent.

source.place: First two paragraphs: canonical proper/open automorphism-square exchanges; with the canonical derived shift identifications in the first proof step of lem-zl-weil-shriek-shift-compatibility and Stacks 014E, 0941, 099N(5).

proof.text: Integral shifts: obtain normalized signed chain and descended integral comparisons from automorphismConstructibleStage_integral_shifts, specializing its irrelevant automorphism parameters to the empty scheme. The existence conjunct ranges over all schemes, so no invertibility hypothesis is added to the original assertion. Two normalized chain shifts agree degreewise by the two mapping-cocone coprojections. Good-representative localization is a localization; natural-transformation extensionality through it, followed by cancellation of the shifted retained comparison, proves uniqueness of the descended integral shift.

Rational and common-stage shifts: the same existing automorphism theorem supplies normalized descended shifts for the identity automorphisms of source and target. Uniqueness of the integral shift identifies its constructible restriction through the fully faithful inclusion. Every rational object is the wrapper of an integral object. Every common-stage object lies in its own finite stage. Therefore the prescribed component at shift one determines each natural isomorphism. The zero and addition CommShift laws, induction on nonnegative and negative integers, and faithfulness of the shift by one determine the full CommShift structure uniquely.

fieldRationalPullComp_existsUnique. Use the prescribed object and pure-tensor action of rationalDerivedPullback to identify its copied object action with the integral pullback. Apply raw scalar localization componentwise to the natural isomorphism supplied by integralPullbackComposition. Naturality follows on pure tensors from integral naturality and the localized composition formula, then on all arrows by tensor induction and additivity. Undo the object identifications; the component is heterogeneously equal to the localized integral component. Every rational object is an integral object with its wrapper, so this component equation proves uniqueness by natural-transformation extensionality.

fieldWeilExchange_isIso. Specialize semilinearFieldOperationLifts to the identity morphism of each scheme, with algebraic closure of Q_l, and extract the rational geometric-Frobenius IsEquivalence fields. For the specified proper mate apply CategoryTheory.isIso_mateEquiv_of_isEquivalence. For the specified inverse open mate pass to opposite categories and opposite adjunctions, apply the same theorem, and reflect invertibility back from opposites. No change is made to either exchange map or its adjunction.

Finite proper/open adjunctions: restrict the whole-system pullback/direct-image adjunction using fully faithful reduction of complete constructible objects, as in sfIntegralPullbackLinearAdjunction. This gives additive, integral-linear pullback and direct image. For an open immersion use openFactorCoherence on its identity base-change square. Its completion-unit comparison identifies ordinary restriction with the specified integral pullback on complete constructible inputs. The normalized qcqs realization for the compactification (j,id), followed by removal of identity direct image, identifies the recorded integral support functor with ordinary extension. Restrict the ordinary open adjunction along the full inclusions. Tensor-localize the integral Hom adjunctions; the pure-tensor uniqueness characterization identifies the localized pullback with rationalDerivedPullback. Apply to the geometric fibre maps, using base-change stability of properness and open immersions.

Recorded compact support: for a proper map, the normalized whole-system compact realization for (id,p) removes the identity open extension by uniqueness of left adjoints. This identifies the recorded integral support functor with the actual direct-image functor, so the existing constructible direct-image adjunction localizes to its rational version. Uniqueness of right adjoints identifies fieldWeilProper with that recorded proper support; uniqueness of left adjoints similarly identifies fieldWeilOpen with recorded open support. Whisker these two comparisons, then apply sfFieldShriekCompositionRational for the geometric open and proper factors and the arbitrarily supplied geometric compactification, transported only along the geometric factorization equality. The composition theorem includes independence of compactifications. This yields the natural comparison without separatedness of either structure morphism.

proof_origin.place: Geometric pullback shifts and proper/open adjunction construction; normalized signed shift existence is reused from the existing automorphism-stage interface, with uniqueness proved by coordinates, localization and integer induction. Recorded finite support is identified by adjunction uniqueness and the qcqs compactification compositor.
